prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1279; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was operating a sedan southbound when the vehicle came into contact head-on with a second sedan, identified as operated by Driver 2, in a low-speed collision at an intersection in Pasadena, Texas. Driver 1 stated that a passenger was seated in the front right position at the time of impact. Officers on scene confirmed the presence of the passenger in the vehicle, and no contrary account was offered by either driver. Driver 1 reported back strain and said pain began shortly after the impact. It is not yet clear whether this injury was caused by this collision, and no medical findings have been produced at this time. Scene photographs confirm the general positioning of both vehicles and visible damage to the front ends. However, it is not clear whether all of the damage observed came from this impact. No prior damage to either vehicle is known to the reporting officer. No independent witnesses were located, and the account rests on the statements of the drivers and the physical evidence photographed on scene. Driver 1 is named on the insurance policy covering the sedan involved.
